title: Ignition Interlock Device Program participants and Fund finances

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

1. The number of active participants in the Ignition Interlock Device Program (S.C. Code 56-5-2941) at the end of each month, January 2024 through the most recent month available, separating DUI/DUAC conviction participants from implied consent (56-5-2951) participants if available.
2. The number of drivers eligible for the program at the end of each month for the same period, if tracked. The FY2024 Accountability Report gave 22,660 eligible and 1,211 enrolled as of June 30, 2024.
3. For FY2022 through FY2026: annual receipts of the Ignition Interlock Device Fund (service-provider fees under 56-5-2941(G) and manufacturer certification fees), and annual spending from the Fund by category (for example, devices for indigent drivers, staff, administration).
4. The number of indigency determinations approved and denied under 56-5-2941(F) each year, FY2022 through FY2026.

I am asking only for counts, totals, reports and policies, not any names or other personal information. If an existing report or routine query already shows this, that is all I need; if the exact breakdown does not exist, please send the closest existing records. If any part is exempt, please release the rest and cite the exemption.

Please provide the records electronically (email or download link), in their existing format; spreadsheet or CSV is best for data.

I request a fee waiver or reduction under S.C. Code Section 30-4-30(B), because this information primarily benefits the general public: it shows how a state program affecting thousands of South Carolina drivers works and is funded. It is not for commercial use. If fees will exceed $25, please send an estimate before doing the work.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Lowcountry Records Project

title: Lawful presence verification for non-commercial licenses and IDs, 2022-2026

communications.subject: South Carolina Public Records Law Request: Lawful presence verification for non-commercial licenses and IDs, 2022-2026
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the South Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records about how SCDMV verifies lawful presence for non-U.S. citizens applying for non-commercial driver's licenses, beginner's permits and ID cards (S.C. Code 56-1-40(7); 6 CFR Part 37):

1. SCDMV's current written policies, procedures or desk manuals for verifying lawful presence, including use of the federal SAVE system.
2. For each year 2022 through 2026 to date: the number of SAVE verification queries submitted for license, permit and ID applicants; the number returned verified; the number sent for additional verification; and the number of applications denied because lawful presence could not be verified.
3. The number of non-commercial licenses or IDs cancelled or recalled each year, 2022 through 2026, because the holder was found not lawfully present or the credential was issued in error.
4. Any internal audit, quality review or error report from 2022 to the present on lawful presence verification for non-commercial credentials.
5. Any audit, review, finding or compliance letter from a federal agency (for example DHS, USCIS/SAVE, the DHS Office of Inspector General, GAO, or FMCSA as it relates to non-commercial credentials) from 2022 to the present on SCDMV's lawful presence verification or REAL ID compliance, and SCDMV's response.

title: Aggregate implied consent test and refusal counts; DataMaster policies
